Subject: Private deployment onboarding — environment activation & preflight rundown

Hi Amy / Greenbridge team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Private. Ahead of our technical kickoff next week, I wanted to share a concise preflight rundown so we can avoid last-minute blocks. Attached is the Redwood Private onboarding checklist (v1.2) — please confirm the items below and return the network allowlist when you have it. If anything needs a deeper discussion we can slot an extra 30-min deep-dive with Vivek and Karthik.

High-level asks (please confirm in your reply):
- Network CIDRs we should expect to peer with (preferred in CSV or RFC1918 ranges).
- Public egress constraints and approved outbound IPs for telemetry/health probes.
- KMS provider and key rotation window (we support AWS KMS / GCP KMS / customer HSM).
- Service account model: central SAs vs tenant-scoped SAs and whether you require RBAC mapping.
- Preferred HA/failover region and any internal firewall appliances we need to integrate with.

Attachments referenced: redwood_private_onboarding_checklist_v1.2.pdf, network-allowlist.csv (template).

Next steps: if we get the allowlist + KMS provider by EOD Thursday (11/09) we can confirm a staging activation on Tuesday 11/14.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Amy Reynolds <amy@permacare.ai>

Date: 2028-11-09T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding — environment activation & preflight rundown

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — receiving the checklist now. A couple quick answers and we have a few follow-ups: 

1) Network CIDRs: we can push a CSV by EOD — internal ranges are 10.12.0.0/16 and 10.13.0.0/16.
2) Egress: outbound is routed through our corporate NAT; we'll need the list of destination FQDNs/IPs for telemetry and health checks.
3) KMS: we plan to use AWS KMS (alias/greenbridge-keys) and may require an HSM-backed CMK for production.
4) Service accounts: prefer tenant-scoped SAs for separation.
5) HA region: primary in us-west-2, failover us-east-1. We have an inline firewall that performs TLS inspection on outbound — I will confirm whether exceptions are needed.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you provide the minimum required ports + protocols for the runtime and the L4 VIP?
- We have a compliance window: production cutover must be after 11/20. Staging before 11/14 is fine.

I'll attach the allowlist CSV shortly.

Thanks,
Amy Reynolds
Director, Infrastructure Operations (on behalf of Greenbridge IT)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding — environment activation & preflight rundown

Amy — thanks for the quick responses. Adding a few technical clarifications so your networking team can map inbound/outbound rules: 

Minimum ports/protocols (staging -> production same set):
- 443/TCP (HTTPS) inbound to the L4 load balancer VIP (TLS termination performed at customer gateway or Redwood depending on deployment mode).
- 10250/TCP (control plane) from Redwood control IPs — used for health and config sync (we'll supply exact IPs via network-allowlist.csv).
- 50051/TCP (gRPC) between runtime nodes within the VPC for model shard comms (internal-only).
- 22/TCP only for managed support jumpbox (optional; strict allowlist).

Networking notes:
- We prefer that Greenbridge peer the tenant VPC via AWS Transit Gateway (if possible) or VPC peering for single-account setups.
- For on-prem customers using direct connect/HA circuits, ensure BGP advertisement includes the tenant CIDR and allow asymmetric routing for health probes.
- NAT egress: outbound to telemetry.redwood.ai and metrics.redwood.ai (IPs provided in allowlist) — recommend allowing FQDNs at firewall layer if TLS inspection blocks SNI.

KMS guidance: see attached kms-guidance.pdf for recommended CMK policy and cross-account access. If you opt for HSM-backed keys we'll need a KMS role to be provisioned with the decrypt/encrypt privileges for our service principal.

I'll attach a filled example of network-allowlist.csv and the KMS guidance. Marissa: when you have a staging activation window, we'll schedule the infra runbook and smoke tests.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
